source.title: Preserving Plasticity in Continual Learning with Adaptive Linearity Injection
source.citation: Seyed Roozbeh Razavi Rohani et al., 2025
source.authors: Seyed Roozbeh Razavi Rohani; Khashayar Khajavi; Wesley Chung; Mo Chen; Sharan Vaswani

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some figure labels and plotted values are garbled or not recoverable from the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests plasticity on random-label and pixel-permuted image benchmarks in continual-learning settings, which extend the claim to repeated tasks rather than a single training run.
record.gate_note: The paper reports average online training accuracy for random-label tasks and states that the fully continual baseline suffers severe plasticity loss. Figure-only curves are not precise evidence of zero error on an individual randomized dataset. Its permuted-MNIST benchmark reports continual task accuracy, not whether one model fits shuffled or independently permuted inputs to zero training error. The cited original studies are prior work, not this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The random-label and fixed pixel-permutation experiments measure training accuracy in a new, continual-learning setting and bear on V1 and V3. However, accuracy averaged throughout training cannot establish whether final training error reaches zero or remains above zero.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that AdaLin mitigates plasticity loss across their continual-learning benchmarks and that neuron-level adaptation is important for its performance. They do not conclude that these experiments establish zero training error on random labels or unstructured inputs.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates continual supervised learning over repeated tasks with average online training accuracy, rather than the original single-task random-label fitting setup. It uses a hyperparameter sweep and compares standard ReLU networks with modified activation methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by task and method; the authors report severe plasticity loss for the baseline on random-label MNIST and CIFAR-10, and that only neuron-level adaptation fully mitigates loss in the reported granularity ablation.

fits_no_version.finding: Baseline random-label online accuracy deteriorates over successive tasks, while AdaLin preserves continual trainability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Repeated random-label training can reduce subsequent trainability, and adaptive activations can mitigate this decline.

record.problems: The evidence relevant to these versions is primarily plotted continual-task accuracy without recoverable numeric values. The reported metric is average online task accuracy, not explicit zero training error or test error at chance for a single randomized labeling. Hyperparameters were selected by a sweep for each method–benchmark pair, so the paper does not directly establish unchanged hyperparameters across true-label and random-label fits.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Other results concern distinct plasticity benchmarks or comparisons and do not measure the behaviors named by the tested claim versions.

untested.parts: Final zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance on random-label tasks, and a matched true-label comparison establishing unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence as the corrupted-label fraction increases.
Final zero training error on fixed-permutation inputs; independently permuted images and Gaussian-noise inputs.
A corruption-fraction sweep measuring perfect training fit and progressively worsening test error.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting and whether removing them impairs true-label generalization. The L2 plasticity comparison does not resolve these questions.
Within-training learning order for shared real patterns versus noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict label is warranted from the supplied evidence: declining or sustained online accuracy does not resolve the versions' endpoint fitting claims. An online average below one can coexist with perfect final fitting. Exact curve values and final fitting outcomes should not be inferred from axis labels or qualitative plasticity statements.

versions.untested_parts: The paper studies repeated random-label tasks and reports average online training accuracy, but does not state zero or near-zero training error, test error at chance, or whether fitting one random labeling required unchanged hyperparameters.
Training time to fit true versus random labels and convergence as corruption increases are not reported.

Permuted MNIST is a continual sequence with a fixed pixel permutation per task; the paper does not report zero training error for shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
No sweep over fractions of randomly corrupted labels or corresponding training and test errors is reported.

The paper includes an L2 baseline in some benchmarks but does not test whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent random-label fitting or whether their removal worsens true-label generalization.
The paper does not compare learning order for real versus random labels over training.

rows.subject: Baseline
rows.size_stated: two-layer MLP with 100 hidden units per layer
rows.operation_detail: trained on 250 successive Random Label MNIST tasks, each with newly randomized labels
rows.measure: average task accuracy / average online train accuracy
rows.value: figure only; authors state the Baseline suffers from severe plasticity loss
rows.uncertainty: three additional seeds; shaded regions represent one standard deviation
rows.note: Continual-task accuracy measures sustained learning on repeated randomized targets, not zero training error for one random labeling. Exact plotted values are not available in the text.
rows.check: Severe decline in average online training accuracy establishes reduced continual trainability, but does not establish incomplete fitting at the end of each task. Replace the partial state; final training error is unavailable.

rows.operation_detail: trained on 250 successive Random Label MNIST tasks, each with newly randomized labels

relation.reason: Its own experiments measure training accuracy on random-label and permuted-input tasks, bearing on continual trainability, although they cannot establish the final fitting requirements of V1 or V3.

tranche.reason: The study measures learning of randomized labels and shared pixel permutations in a new continual-learning setting. Its online accuracy results leave final interpolation undetermined.

source_check.notes: Average online training accuracy averages batch accuracies throughout each task; it does not establish terminal training error or chance test performance. R5's statement concerns baseline methods across benchmarks, not specifically a decline of Baseline on Permuted MNIST.
